During the debate, few people were present in the chamber.
A colleague approached me asking if I could help her daughter who had a dislodged tooth.
The child’s permanent tooth had erupted adjacent to a retained baby tooth without shedding it.
The child had eaten garlic bread prior to the incident, which contributed to trauma causing the tooth to become lodged.
The tooth was damaged and developed a small hematoma, making it painful and sensitive to touch.
I used a frozen Snickers bar as a makeshift dental tool to remove the tooth.
I applied ice to the area for five minutes to induce temporary numbing effect.
After two attempts with the frozen candy, the tooth successfully detached and was removed manually.

The act of helping someone in distress is morally justified regardless of legal risk.

Sharing personal anecdotes involving improvisation enhances credibility and relatability in storytelling.
